title: Altinn Studio — Observability
description: Health of the Victoria observability stack in Studio prod (namespace observability): the metrics, logs and traces storage pairs (copies a and b), observability-proxy in front of them, the agents replicating to them, and the VictoriaMetrics operator. From the stack's own metrics, scraped every 30 s by vmagent-self into the stack itself.

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: Targets of vmagent-self that answered (up) and did not (down) at the last scrape: two copies of each storage, two replicas of each agent, the operator, vmagent-self and the proxy replicas. With no data at all, vmagent-self or the metrics storage is down.

panels.title: Scrape targets over time
panels.description: up per scrape target, every 30 s. The storage targets are the two copies (…-a, …-b) of each signal; the agents are scraped per replica. The proxy replicas are scraped by pod address (observability-proxy <pod IP>:9090), so a replaced pod is a new row.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: Process restarts per target: process_start_time_seconds is later than its last value in the hour before, so a restart after downtime counts too. A storage copy or agent replica that restarts repeatedly is crash-looping or being OOM-killed; see Memory against the limit below. The proxy reports no start time: a restarted container shows as its CPU time counter starting over, a replaced pod in Proxy replicas up.

panels.title: Proxy replicas up
panels.description: observability-proxy replicas that answered vmagent-self's last scrape; Studio prod runs 2. vmagent-self finds the replicas through DNS, so a pod that is gone drops out of the count instead of showing as down.

panels.title: Ingest requests per source
panels.description: OTLP writes per second through the proxy, per source identity and status: 2xx and 5xx as classes, other codes as they are. 401 (no identity: missing or unknown token), 403, 413 (body too large), 429 (rate limited) and 5xx are refused or failed writes; a collector retries them. 499 is a client that gave up before the response started.

panels.title: Query requests per source
panels.description: Reads per second through the proxy (Grafana's datasources), per source identity and status, as for ingest. Grafana cancels queries it no longer needs, which shows as 499.

panels.title: Token slot per source
panels.description: Requests per second by the token each source identity presented: current or previous. During a token rotation, previous should fall to zero before the old token is removed.

panels.title: Authentication failures
panels.description: Requests refused with 401, by reason: missing_bearer_token (no Authorization header, or another scheme) or unknown_token (a token the proxy does not accept, such as one removed too early in a rotation).

panels.title: Rate-limit rejections
panels.description: Requests refused with 429 by the proxy's own per-identity limit, per replica window (a 429 passed through from a backend is not counted here).

panels.title: Forwarding errors
panels.description: Requests the proxy could not forward, or not completely, on the backend's or the proxy's side, by destination (agent for writes, storage copy a or b for reads), signal and YARP error type. Requests a client cancelled are not counted.

panels.title: Read destination per replica
panels.description: The storage copy each proxy replica sends a signal's reads to. Reads go to copy a until it fails a health check, then move to b and stay there until the replica restarts, even after a is healthy again: b (standby). Only a read moves a replica, so one that served no read while a was down shows b only during the outage and a again afterwards.

targets.expr: max by (service_instance_id, altinn_observability_proxy_signal) (altinn_observability_proxy_read_destination_active{job="observability-proxy", altinn_observability_proxy_destination="a"}) + 2 * max by (service_instance_id, altinn_observability_proxy_signal) (altinn_observability_proxy_read_destination_active{job="observability-proxy", altinn_observability_proxy_destination="b"})

panels.title: Read destination health
panels.description: Whether each storage copy passes the proxy's health checks, per signal: unhealthy when any replica sees it fail.

panels.title: Read failovers
panels.description: Moves of a signal's reads from one storage copy to the other, per replica, by the copy the reads moved to.

panels.title: Request duration
panels.description: 95th and 99th percentile of the proxy's request duration, per direction and signal, including the time the backend took.

panels.title: Backend request duration
panels.description: 99th percentile of the proxy's requests to each backend: the agents for writes, the storage copies for reads and their health checks. A live tail of logs is one long request and raises the read percentiles while it runs.

panels.title: Metrics ingest per copy
panels.description: Per second, samples written to each VMSingle (vm_rows_inserted_total). The agents write everything to both copies, so the two lines should match; a gap means one copy is behind (its agent queue grows) or missing data.

panels.title: Logs ingest per copy
panels.description: Per second, log entries written to each VLSingle (vl_rows_ingested_total). The agents write everything to both copies, so the two lines should match; a gap means one copy is behind (its agent queue grows) or missing data.

panels.title: Traces ingest per copy
panels.description: Per second, spans written to each VTSingle (vt_rows_ingested_total, without the trace index rows the storage adds itself). The agents write everything to both copies, so the two lines should match; a gap means one copy is behind (its agent queue grows) or missing data.

panels.title: Agent queue per copy
panels.description: Data each agent holds for a storage copy it cannot write to yet (in memory and in its on-disk queue), for the replica holding the most. Each replica queues up to 20 GiB per copy (maxDiskUsagePerURL) on its 50 GiB volume and then drops the oldest data. Copy a is the first remote-write URL (1:secret-url), copy b the second.

targets.expr: max by (job, copy) (label_replace(label_replace(max by (job, url) (vmagent_remotewrite_pending_data_bytes{job="vmagent"}), "copy", "a", "url", "1:.*"), "copy", "b", "url", "2:.*") or label_replace(label_replace(max by (job, url) (vlagent_remotewrite_pending_data_bytes{job="vlagent"}), "copy", "a", "url", "1:.*"), "copy", "b", "url", "2:.*") or label_replace(label_replace(max by (job, url) (vtagent_remotewrite_pending_data_bytes{job="vtagent"}), "copy", "a", "url", "1:.*"), "copy", "b", "url", "2:.*"))

panels.title: Data dropped by agents
panels.description: Blocks the agents dropped, per storage copy: queue overflow, when a copy has been unreachable long enough to fill its 20 GiB queue (vm_persistentqueue_blocks_dropped_total; vm_persistentqueue_bytes_dropped_total has the bytes), and blocks a copy rejected for good (*_remotewrite_packets_dropped_total). Should be zero: anything here is data missing from that copy.

panels.title: VMSingle free disk
panels.description: Free space on each VMSingle volume (512 GiB) against its floor, -storage.minFreeDiskSpaceBytes (100 GiB): below the floor VMSingle stops accepting writes and the agents queue. Metrics are kept 90 days and old data is not dropped to make room.

panels.title: Days until floor
panels.description: Days until each VMSingle copy reaches its free space floor if free space keeps shrinking at the rate of the last 24 hours. Empty when it is not shrinking.

panels.title: Logs and traces disk used
panels.description: Used share of each VLSingle (256 GiB) and VTSingle (512 GiB) volume. Above -retention.maxDiskUsagePercent (80 %) the oldest daily partitions are dropped, so the retention window shrinks below one year rather than ingestion stopping.

panels.title: Agent queue space left
panels.description: Room left in each agent's queue for a storage copy, for the replica with the least: the queue's 20 GiB allowance minus what it holds, or the free space on the agent's 50 GiB volume if that is less.

panels.title: Rows rejected
panels.description: Rows the storage or agents refused, by reason: too many labels or fields, timestamps outside the retention window, unparsable input, or the VMSingle series limits. VictoriaLogs and VictoriaTraces rows dropped for debug logging are left out.

panels.title: Series limit usage
panels.description: New series in the last hour and day against -storage.maxHourlySeries (4 million) and -storage.maxDailySeries (8 million). At 100 % VMSingle drops the samples of further new series (Rows rejected, series limit) so a cardinality blow-up cannot exhaust memory.

panels.title: New series per hour
panels.description: Series created in each VMSingle in the preceding hour (vm_new_timeseries_created_total). A step up is a new label value with high cardinality, such as an ID in a metric label.

panels.title: Memory against the limit
panels.description: Resident memory of each process as a share of its container's memory limit (process_memory_limit_bytes, from the cgroup). At 100 % the container is OOM-killed (see Restarts). The proxy's working set is set against its 256 MiB limit, which it does not report. The operator reports no limit and is left out.

panels.title: Concurrent queries
panels.description: Peak queries running at once in each storage copy as a share of its limit (-search.maxConcurrentRequests, 8 for VMSingle). Further queries wait, and fail after -search.maxQueueDuration; see Queries waited or timed out. Sampled every 30 s, so short peaks can be missed.

targets.expr: max by (job, copy) (max_over_time({__name__=~"vm_concurrent_select_current|vl_concurrent_select_current|vt_concurrent_select_current", job=~"vmsingle|vlsingle|vtsingle"}[$__interval])) / max by (job, copy) ({__name__=~"vm_concurrent_select_capacity|vl_concurrent_select_capacity|vt_concurrent_select_capacity", job=~"vmsingle|vlsingle|vtsingle"})

panels.title: Queries waited or timed out
panels.description: Queries that found every slot taken and had to wait (…_concurrent_select_limit_reached_total) and those that gave up waiting (…_limit_timeout_total). Waits are queueing; timeouts are errors the reader saw.
